title: Stream epoch snapshotting for stable CUDA graph replay
creator: Ariana Patel
description:
Problem: In mixed prefill/stream workloads we observe non-deterministic CUDA graph replay failures when two or more decode streams capture overlapping kernel segments with different prefill window alignments. Root causes: dynamic kernel selection (kernel autotuner picks different kernels based on transient occupancy stats), divergent KV cache epoch boundaries, and racey graph segment dedup/merge heuristics. Symptoms include sporadic wrong-output tokens, infrequent OOMs during replay, and increased graph recapture frequency under bursty traffic.

Proposal: Implement an epoch-based snapshotting protocol for stream captures. Each stream capture will record a small, canonical epoch header (epoch id, prefill-length-hash, kernel-selection-seed, KV-checksum) that becomes part of the graph signature. During replay, the runtime will validate signature alignment and either: 1) replay the exact captured graph segment, 2) trigger deterministic recapture using the recorded kernel-selection-seed, or 3) fallback to single-stream decode on mismatch. Additionally introduce a lightweight deduplication layer that groups compatible captures by epoch signature rather than raw buffer layout; this prevents accidental merging of semantically different captures.

Design trade-offs:
- Pros: deterministic validation reduces silent correctness regressions, simplifies debugging, and enables safe sharing of captured segments across similar streams.
- Cons: small metadata overhead per capture (epoch header) and additional checks during replay which slightly increase replay-path CPU. We will cap validations under high-throughput paths and sample-check production traffic to keep latency impact minimal.

Implementation outline:
1) Capture: attach epoch header to every graph capture; compute prefill-length-hash and KV-checksum at prefill checkpoint. Record kernel-selection-seed from the kernel allocator.
2) Dedup: replace current memory-layout dedup with epoch-signature dedup; keep fallback for legacy captures.
3) Replay: validate signature; if mismatch, consult captured kernel-selection-seed to force deterministic kernel binding and recapture; if recapture cannot succeed (resource constrained), fallback to isolated single-stream decode.
4) Testing: fuzz harness that replays mixed prefill-length workloads, synthetic kernel selection variance, and preemption scenarios. Add unit tests around signature formation and dedup logic.

Goals: reduce silent token-regression incidents to near-zero and remove nondeterministic recapture spikes under mixed workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Fuzz harness (100k randomized mixed-prefill trials) shows deterministic replay success >= 99.998%
No silent token-regression alerts from sample production traffic for 2 weeks after rollout
P95/latency for decode-replay path increases <= 2% on benchmark suite compared to baseline
New CI tests covering epoch-signature formation, dedup grouping, and replay fallback are green
Rollout playbook with automatic rollback on OOM/latency alarms exists in docs
